title: Drop and Asset
premise: Jude Vasquez, a whistle-blower living under four names, receives a call on a burner phone that shouldn't exist — the voice belongs to his dead handler, Mara, who is alive, compromised, and hiding inside a defector extraction operation. The defector she's moving across the border carries an encrypted inheritance: the ledger of a private intelligence firm that manufactured Jude's original whistle-blowing case. As the checkpoint shift changes loom, Jude realizes the defector may be bait designed to flush out every ghost the firm ever buried — including him. In the end, Jude lets himself be caught to trigger the trap in reverse, trades the ledger for Mara's freedom, and burns his fourth name for good, choosing memory over erasure.
about_author: Cyrus Marchetti is the pen name of a former logistics analyst who spent a decade writing operational fiction from airport lounges and night-shift offices. He lives somewhere unlisted, keeps two passports, and claims only one of them is real.

chapters.title: Four Names, One Bag
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. We meet him mid-routine: rehearsing his cover story in a motel mirror, checking the go-bag by weight, rotating cash. The emotional beat is controlled paranoia — a man who has made fear into housekeeping. A small crack shows when he catches himself using his real first name aloud.

chapters.title: The Phone That Wasn't Issued
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. A burner phone appears taped under his motel room table — a model discontinued before he went dark. It rings. The voice is Mara's; Mara died eighteen months ago in a car crash Jude has never fully believed. The beat is vertigo: grief weaponized into hope.

chapters.title: Dead Air Protocol
chapters.summary: Mara's POV, present tense. She's alive, running a defector extraction for a cutout firm, and she called Jude because the op's comms were built from his old protocols — someone inside knows his tradecraft intimately. The beat is guilt: she used his death as cover, and now needs his living hands.

chapters.title: Checkpoint Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. He maps the border crossing: shift changes at 06:00 and 18:00, a forty-minute window of thin staffing. He calculates what extraction would take and hates that part of him wants it. Beat: competence as addiction — the old life calling like a muscle memory.

chapters.title: The Defector's Face
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. She introduces the asset: Dr. Ilse Brandt, a biometric data specialist whose defection was announced too loudly, too conveniently. Mara suspects bait but can't prove it. Beat: professional doubt curdling into personal dread as she realizes she may be carrying the bomb herself.

chapters.title: Inheritance
chapters.summary: Jude's POV, flashback braided with present. We learn the ledger Brandt carries documents Halcyon Verity, the private firm that scripted the leak Jude blew the whistle on — meaning his sacrifice was authored, not chosen. Beat: rage reframed as inheritance; the past isn't behind him, it's addressed to him.

chapters.title: Two Safehouses
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Jude and Mara converge on adjacent safehouses without meeting, communicating through dead drops they invented together years ago. The beat is intimacy through tradecraft — love expressed as operational discipline, each drop a sentence neither will say aloud.

chapters.title: The Man Who Checks Motels
chapters.summary: New antagonist POV: Wren, Halcyon Verity's retriever, methodically working the border towns, checking motels with a list of four names. The beat is cold patience; Wren isn't hunting Jude, he's herding him, closing lanes one by one and letting Jude feel the walls move.

chapters.title: Shift Change
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. He watches the 06:00 shift change firsthand and spots the flaw — and the trap: cameras that only run during thin-staff windows. Someone wants an extraction attempted exactly when it looks easiest. Beat: the sick clarity of realizing the door is open because you're meant to walk through it.

chapters.title: What Brandt Remembers
chapters.summary: Brandt's POV. She recalls fragments of her recruitment and suspects her own handlers scripted her defection down to the route. Her memory is both evidence and liability. Beat: the horror of being a person whose recollections are someone else's paperwork.

chapters.title: Contact
chapters.summary: Jude and Mara finally meet face to face in a laundromat at 3 a.m., two people who mourned each other. The scene balances tenderness against interrogation — each testing whether the other could be turned. Beat: relief that doesn't quite trust itself.

chapters.title: Wren's Ledger
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. We learn Wren was Jude's predecessor — a whistle-blower flipped and repurposed, proof of what Halcyon does with conscience. His file on Jude includes things only Mara knew. Beat: dread shifting inward; the leak is close, or the past simply repeats.

chapters.title: The Bait Question
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. She lays out the three possibilities: Brandt is bait, Brandt is genuine, or Brandt is bait who doesn't know it. Each demands a different plan; all three end with someone burned. Beat: decision paralysis rendered as tradecraft — the moment planning becomes confession.

chapters.title: Burned Name
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. His third identity collapses — a credit flag, then a knock on a neighbor's door. He moves to name number four and understands Wren is peeling them off deliberately, forcing him toward the border with nowhere else to be. Beat: erosion; freedom shrinking to a single road.

chapters.title: Ilse's Choice
chapters.summary: Brandt's POV. Confronted with evidence she's cargo, Brandt makes her own play: she'll go along, but she's memorized the ledger's keys and will destroy them if handed to anyone but the press. Beat: agency reclaimed — the asset becomes an actor, complicating everyone's script.

chapters.title: Night Before the Window
chapters.summary: Ensemble chapter, short scenes stitched: gear checks, a lie told to a gas station clerk, Wren receiving final orders, Mara writing a letter she won't send. Beat: held breath — the whole book exhales here, quiet before the mechanics begin.

chapters.title: Extraction
chapters.summary: Jude's POV, kinetic. The run at the 06:00 window goes clean for eleven minutes, then the cameras come on early — the trap springing exactly as predicted. They split: Mara with Brandt, Jude drawing pursuit onto himself. Beat: adrenaline laced with inevitability.

chapters.title: The Room With Two Doors
chapters.summary: Climax begins. Jude is taken to Wren — not arrested, recruited. Wren offers the old bargain: work for Halcyon, keep a name, keep breathing. Jude sees his own future in Wren's tired eyes. Beat: temptation as mirror; corruption offered politely, with benefits.

chapters.title: Ledger and Leverage
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Cornered at the secondary crossing, Mara negotiates using the ledger itself — threatening broadcast unless Jude walks out. Halcyon's local chief hesitates: the ledger names him too. Beat: power turning on its owners; the file corrupts whoever holds it.

chapters.title: Letting Myself Be Caught
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. He flips the trap: he accepts Wren's deal just long enough to walk into Halcyon's relay station and trigger the dead-man broadcast Brandt armed — the ledger going public from inside their own node. Beat: sacrifice as strategy; he gives up his last name to buy the truth an exit.

chapters.title: Aftermath, Unlisted
chapters.summary: Brandt's POV. Weeks later: the ledger is fragmentary but radioactive; hearings begin; Wren vanishes into some new arrangement. Brandt testifies under her own name, having decided memory is the only inheritance worth keeping. Beat: bruised vindication, nothing clean about it.

chapters.title: One Name
chapters.summary: Jude's POV, coda. He and Mara meet once more, off every grid, and part without promises. He unpacks the go-bag for the first time in years — not because he's safe, but because he's done living packed. Final beat: quiet resolve; he keeps one name, his own, and dares the world to collect.
